previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, morbid obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, and epilepsy was admitted for worsening left leg swelling, erythema, and weeping lesions, concerning for recurrent cellulitis. She was started on IV vancomycin with pre-treatment for allergy prevention and showed clinical improvement. Her volume status was managed with IV and oral diuretics, and she reported feeling less bloated. During admission, she experienced an episode of altered mental status concerning for a possible seizure, prompting neurology consultation and follow-up planning. Warfarin was adjusted due to supratherapeutic INR, likely influenced by antibiotics. She completed a course of vancomycin and was transitioned to oral penicillin for infection prophylaxis. Discharge included home health for one final IV dose, follow-up appointments, and instructions on weight monitoring, INR checks, and medication management.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus

EXAMINATION:  CT THIGH

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with morbid obesity, b/l ___ edema R >L with a
painful, palpable mass in medial right thigh// ? mass, compression effect on
vasculature

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector axial CT images of the left thigh from the femoral
head to the proximal tibia were obtained without the administration of
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were reviewed.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 8.3 s, 54.1 cm; CTDIvol = 18.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 999.2
mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 1.3 s, 8.1 cm; CTDIvol = 18.7 mGy (Body) DLP = 139.2
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 1,138 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Lower extremity runoff ___

FINDINGS: 

Evaluation of the medial right thigh is notable for prominent superficial
varicosities (4:111), predominantly along the anteromedial aspect of the
thigh.  There is also a larger vein in the deeper subcutaneous tissues of the
posteromedial aspect of the thigh that extends from the external iliac vein
inferiorly to the level of the distal femur (4:140).  There is mild reticular
subcutaneous edema in the distal right thigh (4:208), without a focal fluid
collection.

There is no acute fracture or dislocation.  Limited evaluation of the hip
joint shows no definite abnormalities.  Limited evaluation of the knee shows
evidence of prior ACL reconstruction.  There are moderate tricompartmental
degenerative changes with prominent osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and
medial compartment joint space narrowing.

There are calcified granulomas in the right gluteal soft tissues, likely
representing injection granulomas or other dystrophic soft tissue
calcification (4:12, 40).  Multiple dystrophic calcifications/calcified
granulomas are also noted in the subcutaneous soft tissues of the
anterolateral thigh (09:27).

Partially imaged portion of the medial left thigh is notable for a prominent
venous structure along the posteromedial thigh, similar to the right side. 
There are several right inguinal lymph nodes, the largest measuring up to 1.3
cm (04:50), which may be reactive.

IMPRESSION:


1. Prominent superficial varicosities in the proximal medial right thigh.
2. No cystic or solid mass detected in the imaged portion of the right thigh..
3. Moderate reticular subcutaneous edema in the distal right thigh.
4. Several right inguinal lymph nodes measuring up to 1.3 cm, which may be
reactive.  Clinical correlation requested.
5. Moderate tricompartmental degenerative changes in the right knee.
Please note that this examination is not optimized for evaluation of the
arteries and veins.
